newsitem.title: UK: Bass down as Merrill cuts estimates.
newsitem.headline: Bass down as Merrill cuts estimates.

text.p: Shares in Bass Plc dropped on Friday as analysts at Merrill Lynch lowered earnings estimates for the brewing-to-hotels group, dealers said.
For the current year through September 1997, Merrill cut its pre-tax profit estimate to 722 million stg from 728 million and for fiscal 1998 it cut to 778 million stg from 790 million, sources said.
Its new estimates were at the low end of the range of analyst forecasts. Analysts at Merrill were not immediately available for comment.
The stock was down 18p at 755 by 0907 GMT, its lowest since last November, in thin volume of 736,867 shares.
Sources said Merrill had highlighted the slowdown in the pace of earnings growth at Bass, arguing there was no immediate prospect of the stock regaining its earlier premium rating.
The stock has been dogged in recent months by uncertainties over its planned acquisition of brewing group Carlsberg-Tetley.

A report in the Financial Times newspaper on Thursday said the government would likely impose tough conditions or block the move, the first major acquisition to be considered by trade secretary Margaret Beckett since Labour came to power last month.
The acquisition would create the largest brewing group in Britain with an estimated market share of some 30 percent.
